sentences.en: In this series of lectures about the history of weather forecasting, I'll start by examining its early history - that'll be the subject of today's talk.
sentences.zh: In 这一系列关于天气预报历史的讲座中，我将首先探讨其早期历史——这将是今天讲座的主题。

sentences.en: OK, so we'll start by going back thousands of years.
sentences.zh: 好的，那么我们将从数千年前开始追溯。

sentences.en: Most ancient cultures had weather gods, and weather catastrophes, such as floods, played an important role in many creation myths.
sentences.zh: 大多数古代文化都有天气之神，而洪水等天气灾难在许多创世神话中都扮演着重要角色。

sentences.en: Generally, weather was attributed to the whims of the gods, as the wide range of weather gods in various cultures shows.
sentences.zh: 总体而言，天气被归因于诸神的反复无常，这一点从各种文化中种类繁多的天气之神便可看出。

sentences.en: For instance, there's the Egyptian sun god Ra, and Thor, the Norse god of thunder and lightning.
sentences.zh: 例如，有埃及的太阳神拉（Ra），以及北欧的雷电之神托尔（Thor）。

sentences.en: Many ancient civilisations developed rites such as dances in order to make the weather gods look kindly on them.
sentences.zh: 许多古代文明发展出了诸如舞蹈之类的仪式，以期让天气之神对他们心生怜爱。

sentences.en: But the weather was of daily importance: observing the skies and drawing the correct conclusions from these observations was really important, in fact their survival depended on it.
sentences.zh: 但天气对日常生活至关重要：观察天空并从这些观察中得出正确结论极为重要，事实上，他们的生存就依赖于此。

sentences.en: It isn't known when people first started to observe the skies, but at around 650 BC, the Babylonians produced the first short-range weather forecasts, based on their observations of clouds and other phenomena.
sentences.zh: 人们最早开始观测天空的时间尚不可考，但大约在公元前650年，巴比伦人基于对云层及其他现象的观测，制作出了最早的短期天气预报。

sentences.en: The Chinese also recognised weather patterns, and oy 300 BC, astronomers had developed a calendar which divided the year into 24 festivals, each associated with a different weather phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 中国人也认识到了天气规律；到公元前300年，天文学家已制定出一部历法，将一年划分为24个节气，每个节气均与一种特定的天气现象相关联。

sentences.en: **FRIELISS The ancient Greeks were the first to develop a more scientific approach to explaining the weather.
sentences.zh: 弗里利斯：古希腊人是首个采用更科学方法解释天气的民族。

sentences.en: The work of the philosopher and scientist Aristotle, in the fourth century BC, is especially noteworthy, as his ideas held sway for nearly 2,000 years.
sentences.zh: 公元前四世纪哲学家兼科学家亚里士多德的研究尤为突出，因为他的理论主导了近两千年。

sentences.en: In 340 BC, he wrote a book in which he attempted to account for the formation of rain, clouds, wind and storms.
sentences.zh: 公元前340年，他撰写了一部著作，试图解释雨、云、风及风暴的形成原理。

sentences.en: He also described celestial phenomena such as haloes - that is, bright circles of light around the sun, the moon and bright stars - and comets.
sentences.zh: 他还描述了晕——即太阳、月亮及明亮恒星周围出现的明亮光圈——以及彗星等天文现象。

sentences.en: Many of his observations were surprisingly accurate.
sentences.zh: 他的许多观测结果出人意料地准确。

sentences.en: For example, he believed that heat could cause water to evaporate.
sentences.zh: 例如，他认为热量可导致水蒸发。

sentences.en: But he also jumped to quite a few wrong conclusions, such as that winds are breathed out by the Earth.
sentences.zh: 但他也得出了不少错误结论，比如认为风是地球呼出的气息。

sentences.en: Errors like this were rectified from the Renaissance onwards.
sentences.zh: 此类错误自文艺复兴时期起才逐步得到纠正。

sentences.en: For nearly 2,000 years, Aristotle's work was accepted as the chief authority on weather theory.
sentences.zh: 近两千年间，亚里士多德的著作一直被奉为天气理论的最高权威。

sentences.en: Alongside this, though, in the Middle Ages weather observations were passed on in the form of proverbs, such as 'Red sky at night, shepherd's delight; red sky in the morning, shepherd's warning'.
sentences.zh: 然而与此同时，在中世纪，天气观测则以谚语形式代代相传，例如‘晚霞满天，牧羊人欢喜；朝霞映空，牧羊人警醒’。

sentences.en: Many of these are based on very good observations and are accurate, as contemporary meteorologists have discovered.
sentences.zh: 其中许多谚语基于极为细致的观察，且相当准确，当代气象学家已证实了这一点。

sentences.en: For centuries, any attempt to forecast the weather could only be based on personal observations, but in the fifteenth century scientists began to see the need for instruments.
sentences.zh: 数个世纪以来，任何天气预报尝试都只能依赖个人观测；但到了十五世纪，科学家们开始意识到需要借助仪器。

sentences.en: Until then, the only ones available were weather vanes - to determine the wind direction - and early versions of rain gauges.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，唯一可用的仪器仅有风向标——用于测定风向——以及早期版本的雨量计。

sentences.en: One of the first, invented in the fifteenth century, was a hygrometer, which measured humidity.
sentences.zh: 十五世纪发明的首批仪器之一是湿度计，用于测量空气湿度。

sentences.en: This was one of many inventions that contributed to the development of weather forecasting.
sentences.zh: 这是众多推动天气预报发展的发明之一。

sentences.en: In 1592, the Italian scientist and inventor Galileo developed the world's first thermometer.
sentences.zh: 1592年，意大利科学家兼发明家伽利略研制出世界上第一支温度计。

sentences.en: His student Torricelli later invented the barometer, which allowed people to measure atmospheric pressure.
sentences.zh: 他的学生托里拆利后来发明了气压计，使人们得以测量大气压力。

sentences.en: In 1648, the French philosopher Pascal proved that pressure decreases with altitude.
sentences.zh: 1648年，法国哲学家帕斯卡证明气压随海拔升高而降低。

sentences.en: This discovery was verified by English astronomer Halley in 1686; and Halley was also the first person to map trade winds.
sentences.zh: 这一发现于1686年由英国天文学家哈雷验证；哈雷同时也是首位绘制信风分布图的人。

sentences.en: This increasing ability to measure factors related to weather helped scientists to understand the atmosphere and its processes better, and they started collecting weather observation data systematically.
sentences.zh: 这种日益增强的天气相关因素测量能力，帮助科学家更好地理解了大气及其运行机制，他们也开始系统性地收集天气观测数据。

sentences.en: In the eighteenth century, the scientist and politician Benjamin Franklin carried out work on electricity and lightning in particular, but he was also very interested in weather and studied it throughout most of his life.
sentences.zh: 十八世纪，科学家兼政治家本杰明·富兰克林尤其致力于电学与闪电的研究，但他对天气亦极感兴趣，并终其一生持续开展相关研究。

sentences.en: It was Franklin who discovered that storms generally travel from west to east.
sentences.zh: 正是富兰克林发现了风暴通常自西向东移动。

sentences.en: In addition to new meteorological instruments, other developments contributed to our understanding of the atmosphere.
sentences.zh: 除新型气象仪器外，其他进展也促进了人类对大气的理解。

sentences.en: People in different locations began to keep records, and n the mid-nineteenth century, the invention of the telegraph made it possible for these records to be collated.
sentences.zh: 不同地区的人们开始记录天气状况，而十九世纪中期电报的发明使得这些记录得以汇总整合。

sentences.en: This led, by the end of the nineteenth century, to the first weather services.
sentences.zh: 这最终促成了十九世纪末首批气象服务机构的建立。

sentences.en: It was not until the early twentieth century that mathematics and physics became part of meteorology, and we'll continue from that point next week.
sentences.zh: 直至二十世纪初，数学与物理学才正式成为气象学的一部分；我们下周将继续从这一节点展开讲述。
